# Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)

The code for the PPO reinforcement learning algorithm is adapted from [CleanRL](https://github.com/vwxyzjn/cleanrl/) and [LeanRL](https://github.com/pytorch-labs/LeanRL/). The code is designed as a single file, making it easy to understand and read, and it supports state-based reinforcement learning and visual-based reinforcement learning.

Note that ManiSkill is still in the testing phase, so we have not completed the training scripts for all pre-built tasks yet (some of these tasks are difficult to solve even by RL alone).

The official benchmark results can be obtained by running the script in the baselines.sh file. The results have been organized and published in our [wandb report ](https://api.wandb.ai/links/stonet2000/k6lz966q).

Currently, there is experimental support based on LeanRL, including compiled PPO and CUDA Graphs enabled. The code is in ppo_fast.py. You need to install [torchrl](https://github.com/pytorch/rl) and [tensordict](https://github.com/pytorch/tensordict/):

```bash
pip install torchrl tensordict
```

## State-based Reinforcement Learning

Here are some example commands that can be run to train state-based policies for various PPO tasks that have been slightly adjusted. The fastest is the PushCube-v1 task, which takes less than one minute to train on a GPU, while the PickCube-v1 task requires 2–5 minutes on a GPU.

The PPO baseline does not guarantee applicability to all tasks, as some tasks lack intensive rewards, have not been well-tuned, or are simply beyond the scope of standard PPO.

```bash
python ppo.py --env_id="PushCube-v1" \
  --num_envs=2048 --update_epochs=8 --num_minibatches=32 \
  --total_timesteps=2_000_000 --eval_freq=10 --num-steps=20
```

To conduct the evaluation, you can run:

```bash
python ppo.py --env_id="PushCube-v1" \
   --evaluate --checkpoint=path/to/model.pt \
   --num_eval_envs=1 --num-eval-steps=1000
```

Note that when using `--evaluate`, the trajectory is saved from the GPU simulation. To correctly replay these trajectories using the `maniskill.trajectory.replay_trajectory` tool, the number of evaluation environments must be fixed at `1` for certain tasks. This is necessary to ensure the reproducibility of tasks with geometric randomization (such as PickSingleYCB). For other tasks without geometric randomization (e.g., PushCube), the number of evaluation environments can be increased.

The examples.sh file contains a complete list of tested commands that can successfully run state-based PPO for various tasks.

The execution result of the state-based PPO baseline script is here: https://api.wandb.ai/links/stonet2000/k6lz966q。

## Reinforcement Learning Based on Vision (RGB)

Here are some examples of commands with minor adjustments for training image-based PPO policies. The fastest one is PushCube-v1, which takes about 1–5 minutes, while PickCube-v1 requires 15–45 minutes. You need to adjust the `--num_envs` parameter based on the GPU memory size, as rendering visual observations consumes a lot of memory. All of the following settings should use less than 15GB of GPU memory. The examples.sh file contains a complete list of tested commands that can run visual-based PPO successfully for many tasks.

```bash
python ppo_rgb.py --env_id="PushCube-v1" \
  --num_envs=256 --update_epochs=8 --num_minibatches=8 \
  --total_timesteps=1_000_000 --eval_freq=10 --num-steps=20
python ppo_rgb.py --env_id="PickCube-v1" \
  --num_envs=256 --update_epochs=8 --num_minibatches=8 \
  --total_timesteps=10_000_000
python ppo_rgb.py --env_id="AnymalC-Reach-v1" \
  --num_envs=256 --update_epochs=8 --num_minibatches=32 \
  --total_timesteps=10_000_000 --num-steps=200 --num-eval-steps=200 \
  --gamma=0.99 --gae_lambda=0.95
```

![](../../../../10-具身智能其他仿真工具及仿真前沿/Maniskill详细文档/实例文档/assets/2025-03-23-18-36-39-image.png)



To evaluate the trained policy, you can run:

```bash
python ppo_rgb.py --env_id="PickCube-v1" \
  --evaluate --checkpoint=path/to/model.pt \
  --num_eval_envs=1 --num-eval-steps=1000
```

This will save the video to `path/to/test_videos`.







The examples.sh file contains a complete list of tested commands that can successfully run RGB-based PPO for various tasks.

The execution results of the RGB-based PPO benchmark script are here: https://api.wandb.ai/links/stonet2000/k6lz966q

## Replay Evaluation Trajectory

Getting better-looking videos may be useful. A simple way is to first use the evaluation script provided above. It will save a .h5 and .json file named after the date and time, and then you can replay with different settings, as follows:

```bash
python -m mani_skill.trajectory.replay_trajectory \
  --traj-path=path/to/trajectory.h5 --use-env-states --shader="rt-fast" \
  --save-video --allow-failure -o "none"
```

It will replay the trajectory based on the environment status, enable ray tracing (with "rt", which offers higher quality but slower performance), and save all videos, including failed trajectories.

## Some Notes

- Using GPU simulation for evaluation (especially for randomized objects) is somewhat challenging. We recommend reading [ in our documentation ](https://maniskill.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/reinforcement_learning/baselines.html#evaluation) to learn how to use GPU simulation to fairly evaluate policies.
- Many tasks support visual observation, but we have not yet carefully verified whether the camera positions of the tasks are set appropriately so that certain tasks can be solved through visual observation.
